method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 70 covers K-M 1/2 and sheet 71 covers M 1/2-O, so Avenue M 1/2 is the shared corridor; both sheets letter 'AVENUE M 1/2' in it and, decisively, both print its width '35' inside it (a half-width avenue here, unlike the 70 ft avenues elsewhere: Ave K 73/277, L 1076/1276, M 2079/2284 on sheet 70 all measure ~204 px). Sheet 70 carries the even frontage 3402 3404 ... 3428 and 3302 3304 (west side); sheet 71 carries the odd frontage 3301 3303 ... 3331, 3401 3403 ... 3427 (east side) -- the two faces of one avenue. The cross-street numbering turns across it: 34th St reads 1302 1304 ... 1324 / 1301 1303 ... 1323 on sheet 70 and continues in the 14xx-15xx range on sheet 71. Both faces are drawn on sheet 70 (x=3075 and x=3178, 103 px = the printed 35 ft), giving centre 3127; on sheet 71 only the east face is drawn (x=185, with lot lines meeting it and its address run immediately west), giving centre 185-52=133. Note recorded for review: sheet 71's M 1/2-to-N block is ~900 px where its N-to-N 1/2 and N 1/2-to-O blocks are ~790, which is what the 35 ft avenue plus the outlot survey produces here; the printed '35' on both plates is what settles the width.
